note: Every normative statement of the spec, quoted verbatim. scripts/check-trace.py verifies each quote still appears in the live spec and that every requirement in a testable scope is covered by at least one vector. Scopes: parse (body to message), scan (byte stream framing), encode (program side), store (record set), detect (feature detection on a tty), presentation (how a terminal shows records: out of scope for a library, listed for completeness).

requirements.quote: OSC 7501 ; pairs ST report OSC 7501 ; ? ST feature detection
ST | ESC \, that is 0x1B 0x5C, or BEL, that is 0x07
The body is a list of key=value pairs separated by : and nothing else.
key := [a-z]+
Whitespace around keys and values is removed.
A malformed pair (no =, empty key, or a byte outside the value set) is skipped and the rest of the report is still processed.
Unknown keys MUST be ignored.
If a key repeats, the last value wins.
Free-text values (msg, title) are standard base64 of UTF-8 text.
Padding is optional.
The decoded text MUST NOT contain control characters (U+0000–U+001F, U+007F, U+0080–U+009F), including newline or tab.
A report is discarded whole if it exceeds one of the limits, if its base64 does not decode, or if decoded text contains a control character. Nothing from a discarded report is applied.
A report with no id addresses the root record.
id := segment ("/" segment)* segment := [A-Za-z0-9_.+-]{1,32}
Each report replaces its record completely. A key missing from the report is missing from the record afterwards.
A report whose id does not match this grammar is ignored.
A parent does not have to exist.
Terminals MUST use this relationship for clearing (see States) and app inheritance (see Keys), and MAY use it for grouping.
Root and child records exist at the same time.
Switching between the primary and alternate screen has no effect on them.
requirements.untested_reason: The store has no notion of screens, so nothing can switch them.

requirements.quote: A full reset (RIS) removes every record. A soft reset (DECSTR) does not.
The state key is required. A report with no state, or one the terminal does not recognize, is ignored.
Removes the addressed record and every record beneath it. With no id, removes every record on the terminal.
the terminal MUST drop working and blocked records and MAY drop idle ones.
done and error survive both events.
terminals MUST NOT require re-sending to keep a record alive.
With blocked only, ignored otherwise.
Unrecognized values are treated as absent.
With working or blocked, ignored otherwise.
Absent means indeterminate: the program is busy but has no percentage to report. Anything else is treated as absent.
A record without app takes it from its nearest ancestor that has one.
A value outside the character set is treated as absent.
A supporting terminal MUST reply with ?.
A reply without states means exactly idle, working, done, blocked, and error.
A reply without kinds means exactly permission, question, and auth.
Programs MUST ignore pairs in the reply that they do not understand.
To avoid waiting, send primary device attributes (CSI c) right after the query.
requirements.untested_reason: Needs a real tty; covered by termstate::detect unit tests on a fake reply stream once that crate lands.

requirements.quote: Terminals MUST refuse a report whose decoded msg or title contains a control character
MUST NOT treat either as markup
requirements.untested_reason: Display concern. The library only hands out plain strings.

requirements.quote: SHOULD disarm text direction overrides and other invisible formatting characters when showing them outside the terminal grid.
requirements.untested_reason: Display concern. A helper is planned.

requirements.quote: The only bytes a terminal writes back are the feature detection reply, which contains nothing from any report.
Anything a terminal shows from a record SHOULD say which terminal it came from
requirements.untested_reason: Display concern. One Store per terminal makes the source explicit.

requirements.quote: Terminals SHOULD rate-limit anything a record causes outside the terminal, such as desktop notifications or sounds.
A report that breaks a limit is discarded whole. Check every pair before touching any stored record.
Whole sequence, OSC through ST | 4096 bytes.
The largest legal report is under 3300.
Key length | 16 bytes
msg | 2732 bytes encoded, 2048 decoded. Check the encoded size before decoding.
title | 256 bytes encoded, 192 decoded
app | 32 bytes
id | 128 bytes total, 32 per segment, 8 levels deep
Records per terminal | 256. Terminals MUST support at least 64. When a report would create a record past the cap, the record that was updated least recently is removed to make room.
Terminals MAY map OSC 9;4 to the root record of this protocol.
